There are all sorts of ways traffic can be generated. It's possible that at least most of the people inside these media organizations don't understand or care how it works, as long as a report can be generated showing the impression or click rate sold. The real problem is, tagging on the ads via Omniture, Coremetrics, GoogleAnalytics, Comscore, Nielsen, etc. aren't always set up to audit how the traffic is being generated. The traffic isn't necessarily from the content an advertiser assumes it to be, especially if the company is using a traffic pooling service like Oversee. It could be that 10% of the traffic is from the site the advertiser paid to be on, and the rest is from some domain misspelling, or link that just happens to have traffic that can be sold - for whatever reason. Chinese traffic is even cheaper, and works when the advertiser isn't careful about asking for reports that look carefully at the user's origin. Typically, there's enough traffic "somewhere" to push ad numbers up if they aren't performing and the placements can be sold in an arbitrage fashion. The whole system feels a lot like what people said about Enron. It was obvious to anyone working in the right place - but it wasn't in anyone's interest to listen to those people.
